title: Quentin and the Contact
premise: Odile Crane, a former data analyst for the private intelligence firm Halcyon Reach, blew the whistle on a black-site program that trained operatives to erase themselves from every database — and has been running under four names ever since. When Flight 4471 vanishes from all records mid-flight, Odile recognizes the signature of the program's final protocol and realizes the network didn't die; it went to market. Hunted by the buyers she once exposed and shadowed by Quentin, the last operative she trained before defecting, she must trace the flight's ghost through the very archives she helped build. In the end, Odile burns the network by feeding her own erased identity back into its system, sacrificing her fourth name — and any hope of a normal life — to drag the truth into daylight.
about_author: Felix Sandoval is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade inside logistics systems he now refuses to name. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside extraordinary paperwork.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A sleepless night in a Lisbon boarding house; we learn her four identities, her insomnia since the incident, and the ritual checks that keep her invisible. Emotional beat: exhaustion sharpening into dread when an old dead-drop signal flickers alive.

chapters.title: The Signal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The dead-drop contains one line: a flight number, 4471, and the word 'live.' She verifies it against a program she thought she destroyed. Beat: the sick recognition of her own work being used.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Onboard or tracking Flight 4471, Quentin watches air-traffic screens lose the aircraft record by record while the plane is still airborne. Beat: cold professional awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. News reports contradict each other; the flight officially never existed. She decides to move, breaking her own rules for the first time in three years. Beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin meets his handler in Marseille and learns the erasure was a demonstration for buyers — and that finding the whistleblower is part of the sale. Beat: loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Archive Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She breaks into a decommissioned data center in Frankfurt where the program's training archives were stored, finding her own voice on old instructional tapes. Beat: grief for the person she was.

chapters.title: Recognition
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Following a trail of Odile's tradecraft, Quentin corners her in the archive — but hesitates, because she taught him everything he knows. Beat: the hunter recognizing his maker.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Forced alliance: Odile offers Quentin proof that Halcyon Reach plans to discard its operatives after the sale. Neither trusts the other. Beat: wary, electric negotiation.

chapters.title: Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reconstructing who was on Flight 4471, she finds a passenger who shouldn't exist: a man with no birth record, trained under the program's first cohort. Beat: the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Hiding in Prague, Quentin breaks his own protocols to protect Odile during a sweep, and admits the program never let him sleep either. Beat: two insomniacs finding common ground.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They recover the buyer ledger — governments, cartels, one tech conglomerate — and realize the auction closes in nine days. Beat: the clock starting.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Lives
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. To reach the auction they must become buyers, forging credentials using techniques Odile invented. Beat: dark humor as teacher and student reverse roles.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Memory
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A captured Halcyon analyst reveals the 'incident' Odile fled was itself a live test — she was the subject. Beat: identity shaken to the root.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin discovers his handler knew he'd find Odile; he was always the leash. He must choose between the only family he's had and the woman who unmade him. Beat: quiet devastation.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Six Left
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A safehouse burns; they lose the ledger copy and nearly each other. Odile realizes the network is herding them toward the auction deliberately. Beat: despair metabolized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Auction Floor
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Disguised as buyers, they infiltrate the sale aboard a chartered yacht off Malta — the same charter company that owned Flight 4471. Beat: vertiginous tension.

chapters.title: Lot One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The first lot is demonstrated live: a witness erased in real time on the deck below. Quentin sees his own future being sold. Beat: horror made concrete.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile initiates her plan: injecting her own erased identity into the auction system so the network must surface every record to verify her. Beat: calm at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Everything Surfaces
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The verification cascade floods buyer channels with the program's full history; the yacht becomes a trap closing on everyone. Quentin turns his gun on his handler. Beat: cathartic chaos.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Escaping the sinking operation, Odile loses her fourth name forever — the burn is total and irreversible. Beat: mourning and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Daylight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Testimony reaches journalists and one honest regulator; arrests begin, quietly, incompletely. Quentin surrenders himself as evidence. Beat: imperfect justice accepted.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. Months later, living under a fifth name she chose herself, Odile sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Beat: hard-won, provisional peace.
